newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to mull law against laundering.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to mull law against laundering.

text.p: The Turkish parliament is expected to take on its autumn agenda, starting next week, a draft law aimed to prevent money laundering, officials said on Friday.
They said the law should be passed by parliament otherwise Turkey could face difficulties in international financial markets.
"The draft law should be passed immediately otherwise Turkey's membership in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is in danger," one official told Reuters.
He said the draft was prepared in line with 40 suggestions made by the FATF, set up under the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
The draft law is presently waiting in parliament's budgetary commission, he said.

Officials said a decree in effect since September 4 which required all bank customers to declare their personal ideintity details when they rent bank safes, and deposit, transfer and withdraw more than one billion lira or cash in checques was not seen satisfactory by the OECD.
Analysts say Turkey has been "a land for black money" in recent years due to loopholes in the banking and other related legal systems.
